_note: Placement map for room 14 (Master Bed). All coordinates are ROOM-LOCAL feet from the footprint min corner — exactly what roomkit.place takes. Read tools/roomkit/BRIEF.md first. Author every piece facing +z (south, toward the camera); rot then aims it: 0 = back to the NORTH wall, 90 = back to the WEST wall, 180 = back to the SOUTH wall, 270 = back to the EAST wall.
_windows_note: Windows are built as GLB pieces sitting flush on the inside wall face — frame + blinds + a bright pane. We deliberately do NOT cut real openings: the app's opening panels render a hardcoded teal translucent slab, and the only viewpoint being judged is from inside the room, where a flush window reads correctly.

Ceiling.note: AS BUILT (re-traced room, round 3): vault springing from the 8 ft wall top, ridge N-S at local x 7.5 (centred), PEAK 14.5 ft above the slab. Height above the slab is h(x) = 8 + 6.5*x/7.5 west of the ridge and 8 + 6.5*(15-x)/7.5 east - 10.4:12, 40.9 deg both sides. Anything hanging from the vault must clear h(x); the Ceiling Fan at x 7.5 has 14.50 ft, which is exactly where its canopy tops out. PITCH IS MEASURED, not guessed: projecting the candidate gables with the ref camera and drawing them over the photo (scratchpad/build/cl3_zoom.py) puts the 14.5 ft rakes, apex and ridge line on the photo's actual fold lines, while the 11.75 ft vault round 2 built cuts straight through the wall art ~135 px low. Covers the FULL 15 x 23.5 rectangle (rooms.points is NULL, so that is what the app renders) with a gable at each end - round 2 stopped the west slope at z=16 and left a hole over x 0..7.5, z 16..23.5. Every triangle is wound to face INTO the room, so it is solid at eye level and invisible from above (check with --pose plan: you must still see the floor). TONE IS METERED, not guessed: a downward plane collects almost no light here (0.044-0.060 of scene radiance), so the slopes are emissive-driven and aimed at display bytes through the tone-curve inverse in build/bb2_tone.py - west slope 234 at the eave grading to 222 at the ridge over 6 bands, east 208 at the ridge to 213, against the app's 223 wall. That 14-level break is the only thing that draws the ridge; round 2 sat both slopes at radiance ~1.0 in the ACES shoulder and got 4 levels, i.e. no visible ridge. The GABLE ends are the opposite case - they are vertical walls that collect 0.72 - so they carry their 217 in ALBEDO with only a token emissive; giving them a ceiling-style emissive makes them the brightest thing in the frame. Recessed cans are 0.27 ft outer with a 0.06 ft rim, aperture +10 and rim -16 relative to whichever band they are cut into, at local (3.9,2.3), (3.3,9.4), (11.7,7.0) - back-projected from the photo - plus (12.2,19.0) over the doorway leg.

Baseboards.note: AS BUILT (re-traced room, round 2): white 5.5 in x 0.84 in skirting on the inside face of all SIX perimeter walls — north z=0 x0..15, west x=0 z0..16, main-south z=16 x0..9, east x=15 z0..23.5, leg-west x=9 z16..23.5, leg-south z=23.5 x9..15 with a 3 ft door gap at x 10.5..13.5. No board across the leg->room opening (z=16, x 9..15) — that is the doorway — and the two runs meeting the outside corner at (9,16) are extended 0.08 ft past it so the board wraps the jamb, which is what the photo shows bottom-left. Profile is extruded, not a slab: the face is held FLAT for 4.8 in (0.01 ft off the wall plane) and the whole chamfer is squeezed into a 0.7 in cap, so the top edge is a crisp line instead of a ramp eating a third of the height. VALUE IS METERED, not guessed: build/bb2_tone.py inverts the renderer's response (exposure 1.15 -> ACES -> sRGB), so the round-1 face at byte 199 = scene radiance 0.452, minus its 0.047 emissive = 0.405 of lit term; aiming the face at byte 212 (the photo's measured +24 step over its wall) needs emissive radiance 0.175 = #757575. Measured in the ref render: wall 188, face a flat 212 (+24) over the board's full 17 px, cap 234, bottom AA row 190 — still above the wall. The emissive is standing in for bounce light the app does not render; raising it further would make the trim glow at night (at #757575 it sits ~136 in a dark room).

Bed.note: King. Tall grey panel headboard against the north wall, white duvet with a soft drape, two grey shams plus white pillows, storage drawer at the foot.

Rug.note: AS BUILT (re-traced room, round 2): cream loop-pile area rug, PILE 10.05 x 7.05 ft at local x 2.55..12.60, z 2.45..9.50 (the bbox is bigger because the floor contact-shadow decals reach 0.59 ft past it). 38 real half-round loop rows running EAST-WEST at a 0.1855 ft pitch, 0.028 ft peak-to-valley, so each row catches its own highlight -- measured at the ref camera it now scans mean 200 / sd 9.0 / mean|dY| 2.79 / period 8.0 px against the photo's 189 / 6.7 / 2.61 / 8.6. Serrated on all four edges (rib phase east/west, alternating vertex-by-vertex north/south) over a 0.05-0.12 ft skirt of visible pile thickness. Base #c3c4c6 renders ~207 flat, R-B -2: the ACES curve is so compressive at the old 221 that no rib geometry could show there, so the darkening is what BUYS the texture. NOTE pos.y = 0.004, NOT the usual 0.010: house.js draws the room slab at y 0.01 and objects.js writes pos.y into the same space, so anything seated at 0.010 is coplanar with the floor and its shadow decals lose the depth test -- this model's min-Y is its skirt bottom at -0.028, which puts the decals a clear 0.022 ft above the slab and still buries the skirt in it. Fake AO also hugs the bed's footprint (the app renders no shadows at all); it is keyed to the Bed at local x 4.169..10.831, z 0.155..7.366, so re-run build/j2r2_rug.py if the bed moves.

Wall Art.note: AS BUILT (re-traced room, round 2): coral/red poppy-field gallery-wrap canvas, 5.18 x 4.75 ft — a chunky 1.09:1, NOT the 1.5:1 banner earlier rounds built. The top edge was found by sub-pixel line fits on a contrast-stretched crop (build/a4_edges.py): the photo's canvas quad is TL(237.7,134.5) TR(322.3,112.6) BR(316.3,202.9) BL(236.4,203.9), i.e. mean 82.25 x 79.85 px, H/W 0.971, against a headboard panel measured the same way at 231.5..333.1 (101.6 px). Earlier rounds put the top edge at ~130/119, which is partway down into the poppies — the canvas's top ~12% is bare white ground and reads as wall. Size/height/centre are solved from those photo ratios through an analytic model of the ref camera (build/a4_proj.py) against OUR 6.54 ft headboard, so re-run `python a4_proj.py solve` if the bed changes. Measured back in the render: canvas/headboard 0.806 (photo 0.809), H/W 0.959 (0.971), bottom-gap/headboard 0.222 (0.209). Pigment is authored as PHOTO PIXELS and inverted through the renderer's exposure-1.15 -> ACES -> sRGB chain (build/a4_tone.py, full 3x3 matrices — a per-channel inverse loses ~30% of the chroma on the coral); measured in the ref render the canvas now sits at lum/wall 0.757 vs the photo's 0.756 and mean saturation 0.145 vs 0.150. *** COLLISION, unresolved: Window North (local x 4.18..6.42, casing 0.38 ft proud) sits inside this canvas's span 4.69..9.87. The photo puts the window's right jamb ~1.6 ft WEST of the headboard's left end with clear white wall on both sides of the art, so the window (or the bed) is what has to move — the canvas cannot dodge it without leaving the headboard. pos.z is 0.42 so the canvas's back face clears the casing and the painting occludes the window cleanly instead of the blinds punching through it; put z back to ~0.05 once the window moves. ***

Nightstand.note: Grey two-drawer nightstand right of the bed, with a small white table lamp on top.

Dresser.note: AS BUILT (round 2): grey weathered-oak double dresser + a REAL mirror. Case 4.35 x 2.86 x 1.45 ft on 0.26 ft feet (floor visible under it), top slab 4.50 x 1.58; six drawers 2 cols x 3 rows with a dark reveal line under each and a short bar pull; one grey for case + ends + feet + top slab (the round-1 build was a dark lid on a pale box) with sparse low-contrast horizontal grain streaks. Mirror 3.95 x 3.15 ft outer, 0.33 ft rails, sitting on the slab, offset 0.12 ft left of the case centre; the pane is PALE and slightly reflective (roughness 0.16) with a painted reflection: full-width vault-shadow band top, a blinded window upper-left, a stepped dark band along the bottom -- never a dark rectangle, which is what made it read as a switched-off TV. Occupies local x -0.03..4.47 (slab), the mirror 0.13..4.08. SIZING: the photo profile across the dresser (rows 246-260) is one smooth gradient with hard edges only at x 82 and 152, so all 70 px is the front face and the photo camera is near square-on to the north wall; the ref pose is 27.8 deg oblique (0.884 horizontal foreshortening), so the render CANNOT show the photo's 1.52 front-face aspect at the true size. Built to true feet. TONE: drawer front renders 141 against a 223 wall = 0.634, the photo's 114/182 = 0.63; frame 159 = 0.71; glass 190 = 0.85 (photo 0.88). CONFLICT: the slab's right end overlaps Window North's left jamb (4.25) by 0.22 ft and the bed's left rail by ~0.27 ft -- the 15 ft north wall cannot hold dresser + window + a 6.6 ft king. Window North wants to move east, or the bed does.

Tall Chest.note: AS BUILT (round 2): narrow white/cream four-drawer chest against the WEST wall, front facing east, with the photo's potted plant on top. Case 1.42 w x 3.35 h x 1.28 d; the 4.20 bbox height is the plant. Sits at z 2.84..4.26, i.e. hard against Window West's left edge at z 4.32 -- that is as far south as it goes, and as far as it can go before it stops overlapping the dresser's left end in the ref view (it is 2.7 ft nearer the camera, so it clips the dresser's first ~0.7 ft). Clear of Window North at local x 5.3.

Desk.note: White/light panel-end desk against the east wall under the big window; drawer pedestal at the SOUTH (camera) end, modesty panel between. AS BUILT: carcase is 4.8 x 2.45 x 2.0 ft; the 3.13 bbox height is the tallest bottle of desktop clutter, the desk itself tops out at 2.45 ft, right at the Window East sill (y 2.4). pos.x pulled in from 25.4 to 25.15 so the back rail clears the flush window frame at local x 26.145.

Chair.note: Black mesh task chair on a five-star castor base, pulled slightly out of the kneehole. ROT CHANGED from 270 to 110: 270 put the chair's BACK to the desk. It faces the desk (east = 90) with a 20 deg turn off square, which is what the photo shows. Tall waisted mesh back, crown 3.81 ft.

Foreground Chest.note: Dark charcoal chest of drawers near the doorway — the piece cropped at the right edge of the photo.

Window North.note: AS BUILT: narrow single sash, 2.10 x 5.50 ft of trim (glass 1.58 x 4.72), apron bottom at y 1.80, sill 2.21, glass top 6.93, cap top 7.30. Stands free in white wall in the ONLY clear slot on the north wall — dresser ends at 5.5 (layout.json), headboard starts at 7.7 — with its right jamb at 7.67, exactly as the photo shows it. 2.10x5.50 projects to 1:2.6 in the ref view; the photo measures the window at 28x71 px = 1:2.54. CONFLICT: the Dresser is currently placed at x 2.10..7.10, 1.6 ft east of its own entry above (0.5..5.5); at that position its mirror covers this glass. The dresser has to sit where its entry says for either piece to read.

Window East.note: AS BUILT: the big one over the desk, 5.42 x 4.88 ft of trim (glass 4.90 x 4.10), sill 2.50 so the desk top runs just under it. Blind covers 86% — the uncovered strip at the bottom shows greenery over siding through the glass, as in the photo — plus two small objects on the deep 0.58 ft stool.

Window West.note: AS BUILT: its own unit, NOT a clone of North — wider and shorter (trim 4.22 x 4.24, glass 3.70 x 3.30), with a 0.55 ft projecting stool over a deep 0.46 ft apron board, which is what the photo shows under it. Blind fully lowered.

Ceiling Fan.note: White five-blade fan with a light kit, hanging from the vault. y is the BOTTOM of the fixture (the glass lens). AS BUILT: 4.60 ft blade span; hub is a smooth 48-seg drum d 0.75 x h 0.30 with the blade irons on its TOP rim and one shallow frosted pan d 0.63 x h 0.125 flush underneath — 0.47 ft of hub total, no collar, no globe. Blade chord 0.41 ft, pitch 7.5 deg. The 5.44 ft bbox height is mostly DOWNROD: the vault at local x 11.0 is 14.382 ft above the slab, so the rod runs from the 9.671 blade plane up to 14.382 and a sloped-ceiling canopy tilted 22.4 deg caps it — the canopy rim reaching 14.63 is deliberate, it buries in the slope. Moving pos.x changes the ceiling height above the fan; re-derive the rod length if you do.
